themes.title: Anthropic's S-1 lands; Nvidia backstops the $45B buildout
themes.angle: IPO week turns the AI boom into a public-market test
themes.summary: Anthropic filed its S-1 for a proposed IPO while Nvidia moves to backstop Anthropic's data-centre capacity, including credit support for a $45B cloud project. Markets reacted mixed after a week that also included Microsoft's earnings beat and a softening AI trade. The float is becoming the referendum on AI capex and frontier economics.

items.title: Anthropic files S-1 with the SEC for proposed initial public offering
items.note: Anthropic said it filed a registration statement with the SEC for a proposed IPO; no price terms disclosed in the announcement.

items.title: Two fears will decide the fate of Anthropic’s giant IPO
items.note: FT frames the investor decision as a choice between missing extraordinary AI growth and pricing in risks that include existential ones.

items.title: Odd Lots: What Wall Street Really Thinks About the AI Trade Now
items.note: Market reaction has been mixed this week; a Barclays strategist talks through the AI trade on Odd Lots.

items.title: Nvidia Moves to Backstop a Cloud Provider’s $45 Billion Anthropic Project - The Information
items.note: Nvidia is moving to backstop a cloud provider's $45 billion Anthropic project, per The Information.

items.title: Nvidia in Talks to Offer Credit Support for Nscale Project
items.note: Nvidia is in talks to provide credit guarantees for an Nscale data-centre facility Anthropic plans to use.

themes.title: AI capex meets the earnings test: Alphabet, Intel, Amazon
themes.angle: The market is asking boards to prove AI ROI, not promise it
themes.summary: A brutal Big Tech earnings round: Alphabet lost roughly $500bn in value after admitting AI mode is eating traditional search, Intel fell 22% on a weak PC outlook, and Amazon slid on soaring AI capex with slower commerce. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.4% as AI-spend concerns overtook enthusiasm.

items.title: Alphabet shares tumble in $500bn rout
items.note: Alphabet shares tumbled ~$500bn; it admitted 'AI mode' has hurt traditional search while sales and profit undershot.

items.title: Intel shares fall 22% as weak sales outlook dents turnaround
items.note: Intel fell 22% after forecasting weaker PC chip sales and falling margins.

items.title: Amazon shares slide on lower Christmas sales forecast
items.note: Amazon shares slid on a lower Christmas forecast despite a booming cloud unit; capex is running hot.

items.title: US tech stocks fall after earnings fuel AI spending concerns
items.note: Nasdaq 100 fell 1.4% after Alphabet and Microsoft reported lower-than-expected capex, reigniting the AI-spending debate.

themes.title: Claude 5.5 ships across the stack, 40% cheaper at the top
themes.angle: Inference economics: frontier quality is getting cheaper fast
themes.summary: Anthropic released Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 in one wave. Opus 5.5 leads agentic coding and knowledge work while costing 40% less to run than Opus 5; Sonnet 5.5 is 30%+ faster and up to 30% cheaper. The pricing cuts compress the economics of frontier AI for enterprises.

items.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5.5 Claude Opus 5.5 leads in agentic coding and knowledge work, and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads.
items.note: Opus 5.5 leads agentic coding and knowledge work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads.

items.title: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.5 Claude Sonnet 5.5 is a clear upgrade over Claude Sonnet 5, runs 30%+ faster, and costs up to 30% less for most work.
items.note: Sonnet 5.5 is a clear upgrade over Sonnet 5: 30%+ faster and up to 30% cheaper for most work.

items.title: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5 Claude Haiku 5.5 is our fastest, most capable small model. Built for high-volume work like summarization, subagents, and browser use.
items.note: Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic's fastest small model, built for high-volume summarization, subagents and browser use.

items.title: Investing in the public benefit We’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows.
items.note: Anthropic committed a portion of shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund; that stake grows as the company grows.

themes.title: China's labs turn OpenAI's Astra into a distillation target
themes.angle: The frontier's IP boundary is leaking through OpenAI's own models
themes.summary: The Information reports OpenAI's Astra is now the top distillation target for Chinese AI labs, with DeepSeek and Moonshot said to have used GPT-6 Astra to train their latest models. If accurate, it reframes US export controls and the value of frontier secrecy.

themes.title: GCC: AI strategy approved, data-centre buildout accelerates
themes.angle: Regional governments are operationalizing AI faster than the West
themes.summary: The GCC Ministerial Committee for Digital Government approved a joint AI strategy, Oracle is opening more UAE and Saudi data centres on surging demand, and analysts see Middle East data-centre capacity quadrupling by 2030. The UAE is also rolling out proactive, autonomous government services.
